     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    23	
    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45

Every encoding satisfies it, because then $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)} = g$ as polynomial representatives; a polynomial that is not an encoding need not: for $m = 1$, $d \geq 2$, and $q > 2$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^2$ has $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u$, which differs from $g(u) = u^2$ at every $u \notin \{0,1\}$.    407		then $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \approx_{\delta} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$.
   408	\item If $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \approx_{\delta} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$ \emph{and} $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are projective measurements,
   409		then $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$.\label{item:partial-converse}
   410	\end{enumerate}
   411	\end{fact}
   412	\begin{proof}
   413	Suppose that $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$.
   414	This is equivalent to the statement
   415	\begin{equation}\label{eq:i-derived-a-formula}
   416	\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\bx}_a \otimes B^{\bx}_a \ket{\psi} \geq 1- O(\delta).
   417	\end{equation}
   418	As a result, using the fact that~$A$ and~$B$ are POVMs,
   419	\begin{align}
   420	\E_{\bx} \sum_a \Vert (A_{a}^{\bx}\otimes I - I \otimes B_{a}^{\bx} ) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 
   421	& = \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ((A_{a}^{\bx})^2\otimes I + I \otimes (B_{a}^{\bx})^2 - 2 A_a^{\bx} \otimes B_{a}^{\bx}) \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\
   422	& \leq \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A_{a}^{\bx}\otimes I + I \otimes B_{a}^{\bx} - 2 A_a^{\bx} \otimes B_{a}^{\bx}) \ket{\psi}\label{eq:sometimes-tight}\\
   423	& = 2 - 2 \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a^{\bx} \otimes B_{a}^{\bx} \ket{\psi}\nonumber.
   424	\end{align}
   425	By \Cref{eq:i-derived-a-formula}, this is $O(\delta)$.
   426	As a result, $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \approx_{\delta} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$.
   427	The reverse statement holds when~$A$ and~$B$ are projective measurements
   428	because \Cref{eq:sometimes-tight} is an equality in this case.
   429	\end{proof}
   430	
   431	The following fact shows that we can derive a weaker converse in the case when only one of~$A$ or~$B$ is projective.
   432	
   433	\begin{fact}\label{fact:almost-agreement}
   434	Suppose $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are two measurements such that $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \approx_{\delta} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$.
   435	Suppose further that either~$A$ or~$B$ is a projective measurement (and the other is a POVM measurement).
   436	Then $A^x_a \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta^{1/2}} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes B^x_a$.
   437	\end{fact}
   438	\begin{proof}
   439	Our goal is to upper bound the expression
   440	\begin{equation}\label{eq:anand-is-a-stable-genius-yet-again}
   441	1 - \E_\bx \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\bx}_a \otimes B^{\bx}_a \ket{\psi}.
   442	\end{equation}
